AXP.rationale: American Express presents a solid fundamental-valuation case with a positive skew. Earnings trajectory is strong: +17.6% YoY EPS growth and +9.3% YoY revenue growth in Q1 2026, with operating margins of 33.8% and ROE of 33%. The franchise is durable—closed-loop model, premium customer base with near-100% retention even after a 29% Platinum fee hike, and demographic tailwinds from Millennial/Gen Z growth (70%+ new accounts on fee-paying products). Valuation is constructive: P/E of 20.8x sits near the bottom of its 365-day range (18.4–25.3x) despite accelerating earnings, and the stock trades ~12% below its 52-week high. The Q2 2026 earnings report on the decision date (consensus $4.40 EPS, $19.70B revenue) is a near-term catalyst that could confirm the trajectory. Offsetting factors include OCF deterioration (Q1 2026 OCF $3.80B, down 20.2% YoY), rising leverage (D/E 1.73x, debt up 14.7% YoY), and a macro backdrop of elevated rates (10y at 4.71%) and widening credit spreads. The score reflects a high-quality franchise at a modest discount to its own history, with a dated catalyst, tempered by cash-flow softness and balance-sheet leverage that prevent a higher conviction rating.
